These are my best ten, but only the fifth, eighth and tenth below are cleanly supported by the data.

The most robust pattern in the data is connectivity. When edges 3, 4 and 5 are all `none`, node 3 is cut off from the input (rows 91–96, 100). Setting any one of those edges to a real op then gives huge gains of +25 to +79 points. The effect is much smaller when node 3 is already reached by another path.

Hypotheses 1–4, 6, 7 and 9 rest mostly on that connectivity pattern, and each has at least one weaker or conflicting row. Examples are row 61 for `none`→`nor_conv_3x3` on edge 3 and rows 39 and 72 for edge 5 → `skip_connect`.

Hypothesis 10 is the mirror image: removing the only remaining path into node 3 is catastrophic, as in rows 57 and 59 (about -76 on C10).
